title: Recording: Boil Crisis, Backwards Traveller, Cuff Link by Wings | 1977
content:
Studio Two, Abbey Road Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Geoff Emerick

Wings recorded three new songs on 9 November 1977: ‘Boil Crisis’, ‘Backwards Traveller’, and ‘Cuff Link’.

Before beginning the recordings, Paul McCartney was interviewed in the studio by Alasdair Buchan of the Daily Mirror, and Linda McCartney gave an interview to Maggie Norton from the Hullabaloo show on Capital Radio.

Buchan had asked Paul about his thoughts on punk rock, as had interviewers from Record Mirror and Melody Maker earlier in the week. Perhaps as a result, the first song Wings recorded on this day was ‘Boil Crisis’, a punk-style song that McCartney had demoed in Scotland earlier in the year.

Attentions then turned to ‘Backwards Traveller’, which had the working title ‘Back In Time’. Two tape reels were filled with takes, with McCartney on acoustic guitar and Denny Laine on electric. However, a master take proved elusive, and the song was set aside until 11 November.

Most of the album was the line-up that was when we went to America, with Jimmy and Joe, but there’s a couple of the tracks on it that we did after they’d left, like ‘Backwards Traveller’ and ‘Cuff Link’ where, like, I drummed, for instance, and a couple of tracks I played guitar on, which I mightn’t have done if Jimmy had still been with us.
Paul McCartney
An Evening With Paul McCartney, Capitol Radio, 21 March 1978

Wings then began work on another McCartney demo, an instrumental piece originally known as ‘Yamaha Links (Off The Cuff Links)’. They began a new version, with Paul and Linda on synthesizers and Laine on bass guitar. The new piece, now known as ‘Cuff Link’, was completed the following evening.
